_doc: Iceland, written by hand for the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-12). Same format as todo.json.

areas.season: Cool all year: 10–14 °C in summer with near-endless daylight in June, around 0 °C and 4–5 hours of light in December. Wind and showers any time.
areas.sleep: Downtown near Laugavegur, on foot to everything; tours pick up at numbered bus stops.

items.name: Reykjavík on foot: Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa, the Old Harbour
items.why: The church tower over coloured roofs, the glass concert hall by the sea, and the harbour's fish shacks.

steps.what: The Sun Voyager sculpture and the shore path
The Old Harbour: fish soup or a hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu

items.name: The Golden Circle: Þingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss
items.best: Leave by 08:30 to be ahead of the coaches
items.why: Walk in the rift between two continents, a geyser that blows every few minutes, and a waterfall falling into a canyon.

steps.what: Kerið crater, or the Secret Lagoon in Flúðir

extras: Snorkel Silfra, the rift full of glacier water at Þingvellir, in a drysuit: book ahead.
Lunch among tomato plants at the Friðheimar greenhouse: book a table.
Strokkur's spray drifts with the wind: stand upwind.

items.name: Reykjanes: lava fields, cliffs and the lagoon
items.best: Before your flight home: it's next to the airport
items.why: Steaming ground, sea cliffs, the bridge between continents and the newest lava in Iceland. Ends in a lagoon.
extras: Eruptions have closed roads near Grindavík: check safetravel.is that morning.

items.name: Blue Lagoon or Sky Lagoon
items.why: Warm milky-blue water in a lava field, or an infinity pool facing the ocean in town.

items.name: Whale watching from the Old Harbour
items.why: Minke whales and dolphins in Faxaflói bay; puffin islands from May to August.

items.name: Northern lights outside the city
items.best: Clear nights; check the aurora forecast at vedur.is
items.why: Away from the lights on a clear night, with the aurora forecast.

extras: Check road.is (umferdin.is) and safetravel.is every morning: wind closes roads more often than snow.
Tap water is excellent: no need to buy bottles.
Alcohol is sold only in Vínbúðin shops, with short hours.

areas.season: Mild and windy for Iceland; the glacier often hides in cloud. Summer days are long, winter roads can ice.
areas.sleep: Grundarfjörður by Kirkjufell, or Stykkishólmur for the harbour and the boats.

items.name: Kirkjufell and its waterfalls at sunset
items.why: The arrow-shaped mountain behind small falls: Iceland's most photographed view.

items.name: Around the peninsula: Búðir, Arnarstapi, Djúpalónssandur
items.why: A black church in a lava field, sea arches, black pebble beaches with shipwreck iron and the Snæfellsjökull glacier.

steps.what: Djúpalónssandur: the lifting stones and the shipwreck

items.name: Breiðafjörður islands by boat from Stykkishólmur
items.why: Hundreds of islets with puffins and eagles; scallops pulled from the sea and eaten raw on board.

extras: From Reykjavík it's about 2 h 30: the peninsula is a possible long day trip, but a night makes it easy.

areas.season: Mild and wet for Iceland, and very windy: gusts between Vík and Kirkjubæjarklaustur can close the road. Summer 10–14 °C.
areas.sleep: Vík, or a farm between Skógar and Vík.

items.name: Seljalandsfoss, Gljúfrabúi and Skógafoss on the way
items.why: Walk behind one waterfall, squeeze into a gorge for the second, climb the 500 steps above the third.

steps.what: Seljalandsfoss: the path behind the water
Gljúfrabúi, 5 minutes on, inside a cleft
Skógafoss, and the steps to the top
Kvernufoss, a hidden fall 20 minutes' walk from Skógar

extras: You get soaked behind Seljalandsfoss: waterproof trousers too, not just a jacket.

items.name: Glacier walk on Sólheimajökull, Dyrhólaey, Reynisfjara
items.book: The glacier walk with a certified guide
items.why: Crampons on a blue-ice glacier tongue, then the sea arch of Dyrhólaey and the black beach with basalt columns.

steps.note: 3 h with crampons and a guide

steps.what: Dyrhólaey: the arch and the lighthouse
Reynisfjara: basalt columns and the sea stacks

extras: Reynisfjara's sneaker waves kill: stay well back from the water, watch the warning lights.
Part of Dyrhólaey closes in the nesting season (May to late June).

items.name: Katla ice cave under Mýrdalsjökull
items.why: A cave of black-banded ice under a glacier on a volcano; super-jeeps from Vík.

items.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon
items.why: A mossy serpentine canyon, from the rim path. On the way east.
extras: The rim path can close in spring to protect the moss.

items.name: Þórsmörk by highland bus
items.why: A green valley between three glaciers, reached by fording rivers in a 4x4 bus.

extras: Rented cars must not cross rivers: the highland buses do it for you.
Westman Islands: a ferry from Landeyjahöfn (about 35 min) to puffins and a 1973 lava town.

areas.season: Under Europe's biggest glacier: cold wind off the ice. Glacier walks all year; blue ice caves only in winter (about November to March).
areas.sleep: Near Skaftafell or Jökulsárlón to be first at the lagoon; Höfn has the most beds and restaurants.

items.name: Jökulsárlón, the iceberg lagoon, and Diamond Beach
items.book: The boats run from about April to October
items.why: Blue icebergs drifting to the sea, seals in the channel, and ice shining on a black beach.

steps.what: Amphibian boat or zodiac among the icebergs

extras: Seals fish in the channel under the bridge: look down from the lagoon side.

items.name: Skaftafell: Svartifoss and the glacier tongue
items.why: A waterfall framed by black basalt organ pipes, then the snout of Skaftafellsjökull.

steps.what: Flat walk to the glacier tongue

items.name: Glacier walk on Falljökull
items.why: Crevasses, moulins and blue ice with crampons and an axe. Never on a glacier without a guide.

items.name: Blue ice cave
items.book: Only with a guide; tours go when the cave is safe
items.why: Inside the glacier in natural caves of blue ice that change every winter.

items.name: Höfn: the harbour and a langoustine dinner
items.why: A fishing town known for its langoustine, with the glacier across the bay.

extras: From here to Vík is 2 h 30 without stops; to Seyðisfjörður about 4 h on the fjords road.

areas.season: Cooler and often cloudy, but the sunniest summer days in Iceland come here. Pass roads can ice in any season but summer.
areas.sleep: Seyðisfjörður for the fjord and the art; Egilsstaðir for the services.

items.name: Seyðisfjörður: the blue church and the fjord
items.why: Over a mountain pass into a fjord village of wooden houses, art studios and a rainbow street.

steps.what: The blue church and the rainbow street
The fjord path to the Tvísöngur sound sculpture

items.name: Stuðlagil basalt canyon
items.best: Before the reservoir upstream overflows (usually from August) and turns the river grey
items.why: Basalt columns lining a turquoise glacial river. The east-side path goes down to the water.

steps.what: East side car park: 2.5 km walk to the canyon floor
On the columns by the water

items.name: Hengifoss and Litlanesfoss
items.why: A 128 m waterfall against red-striped cliffs, and a smaller one in basalt columns on the way up.

items.name: Puffins at Borgarfjörður eystri
items.why: A boardwalk on a puffin rock so close you hear them.

extras: The ferry from Denmark arrives in Seyðisfjörður: the village is busy those mornings.

areas.season: Drier and sunnier than the south; cold winters, snow from October. Midges swarm on calm summer days.
areas.sleep: Reykjahlíð on the north shore, near the baths and the geothermal fields.

items.name: Mývatn Nature Baths
items.why: The north's blue lagoon: quieter, cheaper, with a view of the lava.

items.name: Around Lake Mývatn: craters, lava castles, hot springs
items.why: Pseudo-craters, the lava labyrinth of Dimmuborgir, a crater rim walk, boiling mud and a warm cave.

steps.what: Up Hverfjall crater, round the rim
Lunch: geysir bread baked in the ground
The nature baths if not done yet

items.name: Dettifoss and Selfoss
items.why: Europe's most powerful waterfall, grey glacier water roaring into a canyon, and wide Selfoss upstream.

items.name: Ásbyrgi canyon
items.why: A horseshoe of cliffs with a birch forest inside, said to be the hoofprint of Odin's horse.

extras: A midge head net (a few euros) saves summer walks around the lake: they don't bite, but they swarm.
Goðafoss is 40 minutes west, on the road to Akureyri.

areas.season: Sheltered at the head of a long fjord: often the warmest summer days in the north; snowy winters with a ski hill.
areas.sleep: In town, on foot to the harbour and the church.

items.name: Goðafoss on the way in
items.why: The waterfall of the gods, where the old idols were thrown in when Iceland chose Christianity.

items.name: Lake Mývatn and Dettifoss in a day
items.why: Lava castles, craters, boiling mud, and Europe's most powerful waterfall, with a warm bath at the end.

steps.what: Leave Akureyri; Goðafoss on the way if not seen

extras: A midge head net for calm summer days at the lake.

items.name: Akureyri: the church steps, the botanical garden, Forest Lagoon
items.why: The world's northernmost botanical garden, the church above the main street, and a forest spa across the fjord.

items.name: Whale watching in Eyjafjörður
items.why: Humpbacks feeding in the fjord, from Akureyri or Hauganes.

items.name: The Troll Peninsula: Siglufjörður
items.why: Tunnels and fjords to the old herring town, its museum and the edge of the Arctic.

extras: The Mývatn lake circuit is 1 h east: a stop there saves driving back and forth.

areas.season: Cool summers; boats run from about April to October.

items.name: Whale watching from Húsavík
items.why: The whale capital of Iceland: humpbacks most summer days, sometimes blue whales.

steps.what: At the harbour; overalls handed out on board

extras: Even in July you'll be cold on deck: hat and gloves.

items.name: GeoSea sea baths
items.why: Hot seawater pools on the cliff over the bay.

items.name: Ásbyrgi and Dettifoss
items.why: The horseshoe canyon and Europe's most powerful waterfall on the Diamond Circle.

areas.season: Remote and mountainous; roads mostly gravel beyond the main routes. Summer is the season (June to August).
areas.sleep: Ísafjörður, the only town of size.

items.name: Ísafjörður's old town and the maritime museum
items.why: Wooden 18th-century houses on the spit, and a fish lunch at Tjöruhúsið.

items.name: Vigur island: puffins and eider ducks
items.why: A small farm island with thousands of puffins, by boat from Ísafjörður.

items.name: Dynjandi
items.hours: A whole day with the drive
items.why: A waterfall spreading like a bridal veil down 100 m of rock, and six smaller ones under it.

steps.what: Leave Ísafjörður through the Dýrafjörður tunnel
Dynjandi: the path past the lower falls to the foot of the big one
Lunch in Þingeyri on the way back

extras: The Dynjandisheiði road is gravel in parts: check umferdin.is the day before.
Hornstrandir, the roadless nature reserve, is reached by boat from Ísafjörður in summer.
